Proposed repair (production write, NOT performed; awaiting operator approval). Run on the host via SSM against the live MCP container; every step is guarded and stops on the first failure:

```
C=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep '^rebar-mcp' | head -1)
docker exec "$C" sh -c 'cd "$MCP_CODE_DIR" &&
  git diff --cached --quiet e2ed08b343a2be462de4433a93edbb5cbc062a52 &&
  git diff --quiet &&
  test -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" &&
  git update-ref -m "repair interrupted fast-forward" HEAD e2ed08b343a2be462de4433a93edbb5cbc062a52 3835269d792b7764e0beeca95798250487c78895 &&
  test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" &&
  git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main &&
  git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main'
```

Why this is safe: the first 3 checks prove the index and working tree already ARE e2ed08b343a and nothing else; update-ref is compare-and-swap against the current HEAD, so it only moves the branch onto the tree already on disk (no file is rewritten, nothing is discarded). After that the tree is clean and the runbook's own break-glass fast-forward (review-bot-ops.md "MCP code workspace freshness") applies. Expected final line `0 0`. Then re-run the read-only in-container resolution: frontier/standard/trivial should read opus-5-5 / sonnet-5-5 / haiku-5-5. load_config re-stats rebar.toml on each call, so no restart is expected to be needed; that is unverified until the resolution check runs.

## Observed (read-only over SSM, 2026-11-10 ~17:35 PST, host i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

- Live MCP container `rebar-mcp-06b3b1a52303-8093` (image built at 06b3b1a5230, up ~23 h, healthy). Its env sets `REBAR_ROOT=MCP_CODE_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`, so the server reads `rebar.toml` from that workspace, not from the image's `/app`.
- Workspace HEAD = `3835269d792` (2026-10-28 13:48 PDT). Its `origin/main` was fetched to `06b3b1a5230`; GitHub main is now `91182f96362`.
- Running `LLMConfig.from_env()` + `resolve_model_string` inside the container resolves: default model `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`; `frontier` → opus-4-8, `standard` → sonnet-4-6, `trivial` → haiku-4-5. main's `rebar.toml` (after 3340 / `06b3b1a5230`) names the 5.5 models. **Production plan review is not running on the 5.5 models.**
- `git status --porcelain` shows 27 staged entries. The index equals the tree of `e2ed08b343a` exactly (`git diff --cached --quiet e2ed08b343a` → 0), the working tree equals the index, there are 0 untracked files, and `e2ed08b343a^` = `3835269d792`. Index mtime 2026-10-28 17:47:28 PDT; last reflog entry is the 14:14 PDT fast-forward to `3835269d792`.
- The entrypoint's `refresh_code_locked` refuses a dirty tree, so every restart since logs `mcp: dirty code checkout — refusing refresh` (first journal hit 2026-10-29 17:16 PDT). The refusal is stderr-only; nothing alerted.

## Hypotheses (unproven)

The state matches a fast-forward to `e2ed08b343a` that wrote index and working tree but never moved HEAD (process killed between the two). The killer is unidentified: the rebar-mcp journal has no entries in that window; autodeploy ran its 2-minute MCP reconcile throughout.

## Impact

Every production gate that resolves config through this workspace uses the pre-3340 config: 4.x models, and any config key added after 2026-10-28. The 5.5 upgrade (and the Opus 5.5 refusal fix verification) is not live.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The production workspace is repaired by an operator-approved write and reports `0 0` against origin/main (runbook review-bot-ops.md "MCP code workspace freshness"); a fresh in-container resolution shows frontier/standard/trivial on the 5.5 ids.
- [ ] The interrupted-fast-forward state (clean against a descendant commit of HEAD that is an ancestor of origin/main) is either recovered safely by the entrypoint or surfaced loudly (alarm/health), with a test reproducing the stuck state.
- [ ] Root cause of the interruption identified or the evidence searched recorded.

No config key, env var or flag in the fix.
